questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Georgia's Brokerage Relationships in Real Estate Transactions Act (BRRETA) primarily governs:

answers.text: the types of agency relationships and disclosure duties permitted between licensees and clients
the licensing fees and renewal requirements set by the Georgia Real Estate Commission
the settlement procedures required at residential real estate closings
the advertising rules for real estate brokerage firms operating in Georgia

explanations.a: BRRETA (O.C.G.A. § 10-6A) defines the agency relationships available in Georgia real estate transactions — seller's agent, buyer's agent, dual agent, designated agent, and transaction broker — along with the corresponding disclosure obligations and duties.
explanations.b: Licensing fees and renewal requirements are governed by the Georgia Real Estate License Act (O.C.G.A. § 43-40), not BRRETA.
explanations.c: Settlement procedures are addressed in the closing documents and GAR contracts; BRRETA governs agency, not closings.
explanations.d: Advertising rules are addressed in GREC regulations, not BRRETA.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The 'binding agreement date' in a Georgia purchase and sale contract is BEST defined as:

answers.text: the date the buyer signs the initial offer to purchase the property
the date when the last party to sign communicates acceptance to the other party or the other party's broker
the date the closing attorney receives the fully executed contract
the date the earnest money is deposited into the escrow account

explanations.a: The buyer's signature creates an offer, not a binding agreement; acceptance by the seller is also required.
explanations.b: Under standard GAR contract definitions, the binding agreement date is the date the final acceptance is communicated to the other party or broker, creating the enforceable agreement.
explanations.c: The closing attorney's receipt of the contract is an administrative event; it does not determine when the contract became binding.
explanations.d: Earnest money deposit is a subsequent performance obligation; the contract is binding upon communication of acceptance, regardless of when funds are deposited.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia's BRRETA, designated agency occurs when:

answers.text: a broker represents both the buyer and the seller without informing either party
a salesperson is assigned to work exclusively in one geographic territory
a broker designates separate licensees within the same firm to represent the buyer and seller in a transaction
a buyer retains two different brokerage firms to help locate a property simultaneously

explanations.a: Undisclosed representation of both parties would be undisclosed dual agency, which is a violation, not designated agency.
explanations.b: Geographic territory assignment is a business management decision, not designated agency.
explanations.c: Designated agency allows one brokerage firm to represent both buyer and seller by assigning different affiliated licensees as the respective agents for each party, reducing the dual-agency conflict.
explanations.d: Using two different firms simultaneously describes buyer conduct in an open-listing scenario, not designated agency.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: dual agent limited duties under BRRETA
questions.text: Under BRRETA, a Georgia licensee acting as a dual agent owes which of the following to both parties?

answers.text: full fiduciary duties including undivided loyalty and unlimited confidentiality to each party simultaneously
no duty of disclosure about any aspect of the transaction to protect both parties equally
the same comprehensive duties as a seller's agent because the seller initiated the relationship
limited duties that exclude sharing either party's confidential negotiating position with the other

explanations.a: A dual agent cannot owe undivided loyalty to both parties simultaneously; the duty of loyalty is limited when dual agency exists.
explanations.b: A dual agent retains duties of honesty and disclosure of material facts; the duty withheld is sharing confidential negotiating information.
explanations.c: Dual agency limits the agent's duties to both parties equally; the seller's agency does not dominate.
explanations.d: BRRETA permits dual agency only with informed written consent and requires the agent to maintain confidentiality of each party's negotiating position while still disclosing material facts to both.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: In Georgia, the closing of a real estate purchase transaction must be supervised or conducted by:

answers.text: the qualifying broker of the listing firm
a Georgia Bar-licensed attorney
an AMP-certified closing coordinator
the title insurance underwriter's designated representative

explanations.a: The qualifying broker supervises licensed activities but does not conduct closings in the legal sense.
explanations.b: Georgia is an attorney closing state; the preparation and supervision of closing documents constitutes the practice of law, and a licensed Georgia attorney must conduct or supervise the closing.
explanations.c: There is no AMP-certified closing coordinator; AMP administers licensing exams, not closings.
explanations.d: Title underwriters provide insurance; they do not conduct closings under Georgia law.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia law, the seller's property condition disclosure must be provided to the buyer:

answers.text: only after the buyer has completed a satisfactory home inspection
at the time of recording the deed at the county courthouse
before the contract becomes binding on the buyer
within 10 business days after the binding agreement date

explanations.a: Waiting until after the inspection would deprive the buyer of material information needed before committing.
explanations.b: Providing disclosure at recording is far too late; the transaction is already complete.
explanations.c: Georgia's property condition disclosure statutes require that the disclosure be provided to the buyer prior to or contemporaneous with the contract, so the buyer has the information before being bound.
explanations.d: Providing disclosure 10 business days after the binding date is too late; it must come before the contract binds the buyer.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: earnest money held by broker trust account
questions.text: In a Georgia real estate transaction, earnest money submitted with an offer is typically held by:

answers.text: the seller personally until the closing date
the buyer's lender in a special escrow account
the title insurance company pending the appraisal
the listing broker in a designated trust or escrow account

explanations.a: The seller holding earnest money personally creates a conflict of interest and does not satisfy trust account requirements.
explanations.b: The lender is not a party to the purchase contract and does not hold pre-closing earnest money.
explanations.c: Title companies may hold funds at closing but do not typically hold earnest money deposited with an offer.
explanations.d: Georgia license law requires that earnest money be deposited into the brokerage's designated trust or escrow account promptly after the offer is accepted.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: During the due diligence period in a Georgia Purchase and Sale Agreement, a buyer who elects to terminate the contract is typically required to:

answers.text: provide the seller with written notice of termination before the due diligence period expires
furnish the seller with a detailed written report identifying every defect discovered
obtain the listing broker's written consent before the termination is effective
forfeit the entire earnest money deposit as a condition of termination

explanations.a: Under the standard GAR contract, a buyer exercising the right to terminate during the due diligence period must deliver written notice of termination to the seller before the due diligence period ends; no specific reason need be stated.
explanations.b: The buyer is not required to document or explain discovered defects to exercise the unconditional due diligence termination right.
explanations.c: The listing broker has no authority to grant or withhold consent to the buyer's valid contractual termination.
explanations.d: Proper termination during the due diligence period generally entitles the buyer to recover the earnest money, not forfeit it; only improper termination results in forfeiture.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A Georgia licensee who assists both a buyer and seller in completing a transaction without representing either party as an agent is acting as a:

answers.text: seller's subagent under a cooperating broker arrangement
designated agent for both parties simultaneously
transaction broker, owing no fiduciary duties to either party
dual agent who owes limited duties to both parties

explanations.a: A subagent works for the listing side; this is not the same as the non-agency facilitation role described.
explanations.b: Designated agency requires two separate licensees from the same firm to each represent one party.
explanations.c: Under BRRETA, a transaction broker (or facilitator) assists with the transaction without creating an agency relationship and therefore owes no fiduciary duties to either party, only honesty and fair dealing.
explanations.d: Dual agency involves the broker representing both parties with limited duties; a transaction broker represents neither party.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A special stipulation added to a standard GAR Purchase and Sale Agreement:

answers.text: is automatically void unless approved by the GREC before the contract is signed
must be reviewed and initialed by the closing attorney before it takes effect
cannot change any of the printed standard contract terms
generally takes precedence over conflicting pre-printed contract terms

explanations.a: GREC does not pre-approve contract terms; the Commission does not review individual agreements.
explanations.b: The closing attorney's review is not a condition precedent to a special stipulation becoming effective.
explanations.c: A special stipulation can modify pre-printed terms; that is one of its primary purposes.
explanations.d: Under general contract interpretation principles, specifically negotiated terms (special stipulations) control over conflicting standard pre-printed provisions in the same document.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: When a Georgia seller issues a counteroffer to a buyer's original offer, the original offer is:

answers.text: rejected and no longer available for the buyer to accept
held in reserve by the listing broker until the seller decides on the counteroffer
automatically extended for 48 hours while the buyer considers the counteroffer
still valid if the buyer responds within the original offer's acceptance period

explanations.a: A counteroffer operates as a rejection of the original offer under Georgia contract law; once the seller counters, the original offer is extinguished and unavailable for acceptance.
explanations.b: The listing broker does not hold offers 'in reserve'; a counteroffer terminates the original offer.
explanations.c: There is no automatic 48-hour extension of the original offer upon a counteroffer; it is rejected.
explanations.d: After a counteroffer rejects the original offer, the acceptance period becomes irrelevant; the terms must now be re-negotiated.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under a standard GAR Purchase and Sale Agreement, if a buyer defaults by failing to close without legal excuse, the seller's remedies typically include:

answers.text: only returning the earnest money to the buyer as the exclusive remedy
retaining the earnest money as liquidated damages or suing for specific performance
automatically voiding the contract and re-listing the property without further action
filing a mechanic's lien against the buyer's other real property

explanations.a: Returning the earnest money would be a buyer's remedy, not the seller's; the seller retains earnest money on default.
explanations.b: Standard GAR contracts provide that a defaulting buyer's earnest money serves as liquidated damages if the seller elects that remedy, or the seller may pursue specific performance or other legal remedies.
explanations.c: The contract does not void automatically; the seller must affirmatively elect a remedy.
explanations.d: A mechanic's lien secures payment for labor and materials on real property; it is not a buyer default remedy.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: final walk-through right in GAR contract
questions.text: The final walk-through provision in a standard GAR Purchase and Sale Agreement gives the buyer the right to:

answers.text: negotiate a new purchase price if any condition of the property has changed since the offer
terminate the contract based on any subjective dissatisfaction observed during the walk-through
bring a licensed inspector to conduct a new full home inspection before closing
inspect the property shortly before closing to confirm it is in the agreed-upon condition

explanations.a: The walk-through does not reopen price negotiation; its purpose is condition verification, not renegotiation.
explanations.b: Subjective dissatisfaction alone is not a valid basis for termination at the walk-through stage; the due diligence period has ended.
explanations.c: The walk-through is a visual inspection, not a new contracted home inspection; it typically does not include the inspector.
explanations.d: The pre-closing walk-through allows the buyer to verify that the property is in substantially the same condition as when the contract was signed and that all agreed-upon repairs have been made.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: In a typical Georgia residential real estate transaction, the closing attorney is selected by:

answers.text: the buyer or the buyer's lender
the listing broker on behalf of the seller
the Georgia Real Estate Commission from an approved panel
the title insurance underwriter based on geographic proximity

explanations.a: In Georgia practice, the buyer or the buyer's lender typically selects the closing attorney, since the attorney represents the lender's and buyer's interests in ensuring clear title and proper documentation.
explanations.b: The listing broker represents the seller; the attorney is customarily the buyer's and lender's choice.
explanations.c: GREC does not maintain a panel of closing attorneys or assign them to transactions.
explanations.d: Title underwriters do not select the closing attorney; the buyer or lender makes that choice.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The financing contingency in a Georgia Purchase and Sale Agreement protects the buyer by:

answers.text: automatically extending the closing date if the lender requires additional time
allowing the buyer to terminate and recover earnest money if a qualifying loan cannot be obtained
requiring the seller to accept owner financing if the buyer's loan is denied
guaranteeing that the buyer's interest rate will not exceed the rate stated in the contract

explanations.a: The financing contingency does not grant an automatic closing extension; a separate agreement or contractual provision would be needed.
explanations.b: A properly drafted financing contingency entitles the buyer to terminate the contract and recover earnest money if the buyer makes a good-faith effort but cannot obtain the specified financing.
explanations.c: The seller has no obligation to provide financing if the buyer's lender denies the loan.
explanations.d: A financing contingency addresses whether financing is available, not the specific rate; rate guarantees come from the lender's lock-in agreement.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: In a Georgia Purchase and Sale Agreement, the due diligence / termination fee paid by the buyer to the seller is:

answers.text: refunded to the buyer at closing if the transaction proceeds to completion
applied to the purchase price as an additional deposit at closing
retained by the seller in exchange for granting the buyer the right to terminate during the due diligence period
held in the listing broker's trust account and released only with GREC approval

explanations.a: The due diligence fee is not refunded at closing; it is compensation to the seller for granting the termination right.
explanations.b: Unlike earnest money, the due diligence fee is generally paid directly to the seller, not applied to the purchase price at closing.
explanations.c: The due diligence fee is consideration paid to the seller to keep the termination option open during the due diligence period; it is non-refundable if the buyer terminates.
explanations.d: The due diligence fee is typically paid directly to the seller, not placed in the broker's trust account.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: time is of the essence consequences
questions.text: When a Georgia real estate contract states that 'time is of the essence,' missing a contractual deadline means:

answers.text: the party who misses the deadline may be in default and the other party may exercise contractual remedies
either party may extend any deadline by up to 10 days without the other's consent
the closing must be rescheduled within 30 days at GREC's direction
the contract is automatically void and both parties are released from obligations

explanations.a: Time-is-of-the-essence language makes contractual deadlines strict; a party who misses a deadline is in default and the non-defaulting party may pursue available contractual remedies.
explanations.b: Time-is-of-the-essence language tightens deadlines rather than allowing unilateral extensions.
explanations.c: GREC has no role in rescheduling closings.
explanations.d: A missed deadline triggers the non-defaulting party's remedies; the contract does not become automatically void.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A Georgia buyer submits a written offer stating it must be accepted by 5:00 p.m. on Friday. The seller responds at 9:00 a.m. on Saturday. The result is:

answers.text: a binding contract because the seller's response was received before the buyer found another property
no contract, because the seller's response after the deadline operates as a new offer to the buyer
a binding contract if the buyer's agent verbally confirms acceptance of the late response
no contract, but the seller is entitled to keep the buyer's earnest money for the delayed response

explanations.a: A response after the stated deadline is not acceptance of the original offer; the original offer lapsed at 5:00 p.m. Friday.
explanations.b: Because the offer expired at 5:00 p.m. Friday, the seller's Saturday response is not an acceptance of the lapsed offer — it constitutes a new offer that the buyer may accept, reject, or counter.
explanations.c: A verbal confirmation from the agent does not revive a lapsed offer; a new written agreement would be required.
explanations.d: No earnest money was deposited for an unaccepted offer; the seller has no claim to the buyer's funds.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: listing belongs to brokerage not salesperson
questions.text: A Georgia salesperson who obtains a listing agreement and then moves to a different brokerage firm: the listing agreement:

answers.text: automatically transfers with the salesperson to the new brokerage firm
is automatically terminated because the signing salesperson left
remains with the original brokerage firm, because listings belong to the broker, not the salesperson
must be renegotiated between the seller, the original broker, and the new brokerage within 30 days

explanations.a: The salesperson does not own the listing; it cannot follow the salesperson to a new firm.
explanations.b: The departure of the listing salesperson does not terminate the listing; the agreement is between the seller and the brokerage firm.
explanations.c: Under Georgia and general real estate agency law, a listing agreement is a contract between the seller and the brokerage firm, not the individual salesperson; it remains with the original firm.
explanations.d: No renegotiation is required; the listing continues with the original broker.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: multiple offer duty present all to seller
questions.text: A Georgia listing broker receives three simultaneous written offers on a property. The broker's duty is to:

answers.text: accept the highest offer on the seller's behalf without further consultation
present only the two strongest offers to avoid overwhelming the seller
hold all offers until a fourth buyer can be found to create competition
present all three offers to the seller promptly so the seller can make an informed decision

explanations.a: The broker has no authority to accept offers on behalf of the seller; acceptance is the seller's right.
explanations.b: The duty to present extends to all written offers; selectively withholding offers breaches the broker's disclosure duty.
explanations.c: Holding offers without the seller's instruction to wait is a breach of the broker's fiduciary duty to act promptly.
explanations.d: Georgia license law and BRRETA require the listing broker to present all written offers to the seller promptly so the seller can evaluate and decide.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A Georgia seller's agent learns that the property has a hidden structural defect the seller has not disclosed. The agent's duty requires:

answers.text: keeping the information confidential as part of the fiduciary duty of confidentiality to the seller
disclosing the known material defect to prospective buyers
reporting the defect to GREC before showing the property
terminating the listing immediately without any further explanation

explanations.a: Confidentiality protects the seller's negotiating information but does not extend to concealing known material defects that harm buyers.
explanations.b: Georgia license law and the duty of honesty to non-clients require the agent to disclose known material defects to prospective buyers; a material defect is not protected information.
explanations.c: Reporting to GREC is not the required next step; the duty is immediate disclosure to buyers.
explanations.d: Terminating the listing without explanation does not cure the disclosure obligation and could expose the agent to liability.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: duty to non-client honesty fair dealing
questions.text: Under Georgia's BRRETA, a buyer's agent owes which of the following duties to the seller?

answers.text: full fiduciary loyalty, the same as the duty owed to the buyer
no duty whatsoever, because the agent is solely representing the buyer
honesty and fair dealing, including disclosure of known material facts
a duty to negotiate the lowest possible price regardless of the seller's circumstances

explanations.a: Full fiduciary loyalty is owed to the buyer client; the seller is a non-client.
explanations.b: BRRETA imposes minimum duties of honesty and fair dealing on agents toward non-clients; no agent is entirely duty-free toward the other party.
explanations.c: Even though a buyer's agent represents only the buyer, BRRETA requires the agent to treat the seller with honesty and fair dealing, including disclosure of any known material facts about the property or transaction.
explanations.d: Negotiating an aggressive price for the buyer is the agent's role, but it must be accomplished within the bounds of honesty and fair dealing toward the seller.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: exclusive right to sell commission trigger
questions.text: Under an exclusive-right-to-sell listing in Georgia, the listing broker earns a commission when:

answers.text: only when the listing broker personally procures the buyer without any other broker's involvement
only when the buyer is referred by a cooperating broker through the MLS
any time during the listing period when the seller finds a buyer without using any broker
the property sells during the listing period, regardless of who procures the buyer

explanations.a: An exclusive-right-to-sell does not require the listing broker to personally find the buyer; commission is owed regardless of the source.
explanations.b: Commission is owed even if no cooperating broker is involved; it applies to all sales during the listing period.
explanations.c: This describes the exclusive-agency listing, not exclusive-right-to-sell; the seller finding their own buyer still triggers the commission under an exclusive-right-to-sell.
explanations.d: The exclusive-right-to-sell entitles the listing broker to compensation whenever the property sells during the listing term, regardless of who was the procuring cause.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia's BRRETA, the written brokerage engagement agreement or agency disclosure must be provided to a client:

answers.text: before or at the time of entering into a brokerage engagement agreement or when the agency relationship is established
only after the client has made a written offer on a specific property
within 24 hours after the client and licensee first meet in person
at or before closing, as part of the settlement disclosure package

explanations.a: BRRETA requires that the written brokerage engagement or disclosure be provided to the client at or before the time the agency relationship is formed — not after substantive services have been rendered.
explanations.b: Waiting until after an offer is made is far too late; the agency relationship should be established at the outset.
explanations.c: BRRETA does not impose a 24-hour window; the duty is to disclose at or before forming the relationship.
explanations.d: Providing disclosure at closing means the client was unrepresented throughout the transaction without knowing it.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The protection period clause in a Georgia exclusive listing agreement is designed to protect the broker from:

answers.text: buyers who back out of transactions after the earnest money is deposited
other brokers who attempt to solicit the listing after it is posted on the MLS
sellers who wait for the listing to expire and then sell directly to a buyer the broker introduced
GREC audits of listings that closed after their stated expiration date

explanations.a: Buyer default is handled through earnest money and contract remedies; the protection period addresses post-expiration sales.
explanations.b: The protection period does not affect other brokers' ability to solicit an expired listing.
explanations.c: A protection period clause provides that if the property is sold within the stated period after listing expiration to a buyer whom the broker introduced during the listing term, the broker is still entitled to a commission.
explanations.d: GREC audits are not the concern the protection period addresses.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia's BRRETA, a brokerage engagement agreement with a buyer must be:

answers.text: approved by GREC before any buyer representation services may begin
witnessed by a notary public and recorded in the county deed records
reviewed and signed by the qualifying broker within 48 hours of execution
in writing and signed by both the buyer and the brokerage firm before buyer representation commences

explanations.a: GREC does not review or approve individual buyer brokerage agreements before they take effect.
explanations.b: Brokerage engagement agreements are not recorded in the deed records; they are private contracts.
explanations.c: The qualifying broker must supervise licensees but does not countersign every buyer agreement within 48 hours under BRRETA.
explanations.d: BRRETA requires that brokerage engagements be in writing and signed by the buyer and broker before the agency relationship and its attendant duties begin.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia's BRRETA, for a seller's agency relationship to be established, the brokerage firm must have:

answers.text: a written listing agreement signed by the seller before marketing the property
verbal authorization from the seller confirmed by the listing salesperson's written note
approval from the local MLS board before entering into any listing agreement
a signed Sponsoring Broker Statement from the seller to authorize marketing activities

explanations.a: BRRETA requires that a seller's brokerage engagement — the listing agreement — be in writing and signed by the seller; verbal authorization is insufficient to create the agency relationship.
explanations.b: A verbal authorization does not satisfy BRRETA's writing requirement.
explanations.c: MLS board approval is not a prerequisite to entering a listing agreement; the board is for cooperative cooperation, not pre-approval.
explanations.d: A Sponsoring Broker Statement is used in licensing applications; it does not establish a seller's agency relationship.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia law, a landlord who willfully withholds a tenant's security deposit without providing an itemized written statement of deductions may be liable for:

answers.text: the amount withheld plus a mandatory $500 penalty payable to GREC
up to three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus reasonable attorney's fees
only the refund of the deposit with no additional penalty
a civil fine imposed by the Georgia Residential Property Commission

explanations.a: The penalty flows to the tenant, not to GREC, and can be triple the withheld amount.
explanations.b: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-35 provides that a landlord who wrongfully withholds a security deposit without the required itemized accounting may be liable for three times the amount withheld plus attorney's fees.
explanations.c: Georgia law provides penalty damages beyond simple refund when the withholding is willful and no proper accounting is given.
explanations.d: There is no 'Georgia Residential Property Commission'; GREC is the relevant agency for licensees, and the tenant's remedy is a private civil claim.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia law, a landlord must return a tenant's security deposit within how many days after the lease terminates and the tenant vacates?

answers.text: 7 days
60 days
90 days
30 days

explanations.a: 7 days is insufficient; Georgia law provides 30 days to return the deposit or provide an itemized statement of deductions.
explanations.b: 60 days exceeds the statutory 30-day period; failing to return within 30 days exposes the landlord to penalties.
explanations.c: 90 days far exceeds the Georgia statutory deadline for returning security deposits.
explanations.d: O.C.G.A. § 44-7-34 requires the landlord to return the security deposit or provide a written itemized statement of deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant delivers possession.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: When a Georgia tenant fails to pay rent and refuses to vacate after proper notice, the landlord's first formal legal step to evict the tenant is to:

answers.text: file a dispossessory affidavit in the appropriate magistrate or state court
contact local law enforcement to physically remove the tenant immediately
change the door locks and store the tenant's belongings in a secured location
file a lis pendens against the tenant's other real property holdings

explanations.a: Under O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50, the dispossessory process begins with the landlord filing a dispossessory affidavit in magistrate or state court, stating the grounds for eviction.
explanations.b: Law enforcement cannot remove a tenant without a court order; self-help eviction is illegal in Georgia.
explanations.c: Changing locks or removing belongings without a court order is illegal self-help eviction, exposing the landlord to liability.
explanations.d: A lis pendens is recorded against real property in litigation; it is not the eviction mechanism.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A Georgia property manager who manages rental properties on behalf of third-party owners for compensation must hold:

answers.text: a home inspector's license issued by the Georgia Secretary of State
a valid real estate broker's or salesperson's license issued by GREC
only a business license from the county where the properties are located
a certified property manager (CPM) designation from IREM

explanations.a: A home inspector's license is for property inspections, not management; the two licenses are separate.
explanations.b: O.C.G.A. § 43-40 requires anyone who manages real property on behalf of others for compensation to hold a valid Georgia real estate license.
explanations.c: A local business license alone does not satisfy the state licensing requirement for property management services.
explanations.d: A CPM designation is a voluntary professional credential from IREM; it is not the Georgia state license required to manage property for others.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: lease more than one year must be written
questions.text: Under Georgia law, a residential lease with a term of more than one year must be:

answers.text: approved by the local housing authority before the tenant may take possession
recorded in the county deed records to be enforceable against third parties
in writing and signed by the parties to be enforceable
notarized by a Georgia notary public and filed with GREC

explanations.a: Local housing authority approval is not required for a standard market-rate lease.
explanations.b: Recording a lease is not required for the lease to be enforceable between landlord and tenant, though recording a long-term lease may protect against subsequent purchasers.
explanations.c: Under Georgia's Statute of Frauds (O.C.G.A. § 13-5-30), a lease for more than one year must be in writing to be enforceable.
explanations.d: Notarization and GREC filing are not required for a residential lease to be enforceable.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: After a Georgia court issues a writ of possession in a dispossessory action, the tenant is physically removed by:

answers.text: the county sheriff or marshal acting under the court's authority
the landlord's designated property manager without any further legal process
a private security firm hired by the landlord
the Georgia Real Estate Commission's enforcement division

explanations.a: After a court grants the writ of possession in a dispossessory action, the county sheriff or marshal enforces the court's order and physically removes the tenant if necessary.
explanations.b: A property manager has no legal authority to forcibly remove a tenant; that power belongs to law enforcement acting on a court order.
explanations.c: Private security firms may not evict tenants; only law enforcement acting on a court order may do so.
explanations.d: GREC is a licensing agency with no enforcement role in eviction proceedings.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: Under Georgia law, a landlord may lawfully deduct from a security deposit amounts for all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: unpaid rent remaining at the end of the tenancy
normal wear and tear to carpet and paint from regular occupancy
damages caused by the tenant beyond normal wear and tear
costs of cleaning the unit to restore it to its original condition

explanations.a: Unpaid rent is a permissible deduction from the security deposit under Georgia law.
explanations.b: Normal wear and tear — such as minor scuffs on paint or carpet worn from regular use — is an expected cost of occupancy that the landlord, not the tenant, must bear.
explanations.c: Damage beyond normal wear and tear, such as holes in walls or stained carpets from spills, is a proper basis for deduction.
explanations.d: Restoration cleaning costs are a permissible deduction if the unit is left in a condition worse than its original cleanliness.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: To qualify for a Georgia Community Association Manager's license, an applicant must complete a Commission-approved prelicense course of:

answers.text: 75 hours
60 hours
25 hours
40 hours

explanations.a: 75 hours is the salesperson prelicense requirement, not the CAM requirement.
explanations.b: 60 hours is the broker prelicense requirement.
explanations.c: A Community Association Manager applicant must successfully complete a GREC-approved 25-hour Community Association Manager's Prelicense Course before sitting for the exam.
explanations.d: 40 hours is not the required course length for any Georgia real estate license category.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The Georgia Condominium Act (O.C.G.A. § 44-3-70 et seq.) primarily governs:

answers.text: the licensing of community association managers by GREC
the procedures for evicting tenants from condominium rental units
the commission rates that real estate brokers may charge for condominium sales
the creation, organization, operation, and governance of condominium developments in Georgia

explanations.a: CAM licensing is governed by O.C.G.A. § 43-40, not the Georgia Condominium Act.
explanations.b: Eviction procedures for all residential tenancies are governed by the dispossessory statutes; the Condominium Act addresses ownership and governance.
explanations.c: Commission rates are not regulated by the Condominium Act; they are a private business matter.
explanations.d: The Georgia Condominium Act establishes the legal framework for creating and operating condominium associations, including unit ownership, common area governance, assessments, and association powers.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: A Georgia homeowners association that wishes to levy special assessments against members must:

answers.text: obtain approval from the Georgia Real Estate Commission before each assessment
follow the procedures set forth in the association's declaration and bylaws
register the assessment amount with the county tax assessor
obtain a unanimous vote of all property owners in the association

explanations.a: GREC does not approve HOA assessments; the HOA governs itself according to its recorded documents.
explanations.b: Homeowners associations are governed by their declaration, bylaws, and applicable state law; special assessments must be levied in compliance with the procedures established in those governing documents.
explanations.c: Special assessments are not registered with the tax assessor; they are internal HOA obligations.
explanations.d: Most HOA declarations require a majority or super-majority vote, not unanimity, for special assessments; the specific requirement depends on the declaration.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The Georgia Property Owners' Association Act (O.C.G.A. § 44-3-220 et seq.) applies to:

answers.text: all Georgia homeowners associations regardless of whether membership is mandatory
only condominium associations that have more than 10 units
planned developments where membership in the property owners association is mandatory
any Georgia property owner who rents out residential units within a community association

explanations.a: The POAA applies specifically to associations with mandatory membership; voluntary neighborhood associations may operate under other legal frameworks.
explanations.b: The Georgia Condominium Act, not the POAA, governs condominiums; the POAA addresses planned subdivisions with mandatory HOA membership.
explanations.c: The Georgia Property Owners' Association Act governs planned developments in which property owners are required to be members of and pay assessments to a property owners' association as a condition of ownership.
explanations.d: Individual landlords renting within a community are subject to the landlord-tenant statutes; the POAA governs the association structure itself.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: homeowner right to hearing before HOA fine
questions.text: When a Georgia homeowners association intends to impose a fine on a member for a violation of the community rules, the member is generally entitled to:

answers.text: a jury trial in the county superior court before any fine may be assessed
automatic waiver of the fine if the violation is corrected within 24 hours
an injunction preventing the HOA from imposing the fine without court approval
notice of the alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before the fine is imposed

explanations.a: HOA fines are civil association matters; a jury trial is not required before an HOA imposes a fine under its governing documents.
explanations.b: There is no statutory automatic waiver; cure periods may be specified in governing documents, but automatic waiver upon cure is not a general rule.
explanations.c: Courts do not need to pre-approve HOA fines; members may seek judicial review after the fact if they believe the fine is improper.
explanations.d: Due process principles and most HOA governing documents require that the member receive notice of the alleged violation and a reasonable opportunity to respond before the association imposes a fine.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: condominium association governed by Condo Act
questions.text: The legal authority and governance structure of a Georgia condominium association is established by:

answers.text: the Georgia Condominium Act and the association's recorded condominium instruments
the Georgia Real Estate License Act and GREC rules promulgated thereunder
the National Association of REALTORS® Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
the federal Condominium and Cooperative Abuse Relief Act of 1980

explanations.a: The Georgia Condominium Act (O.C.G.A. § 44-3-70 et seq.) provides the statutory framework, while the recorded condominium instruments — the declaration, bylaws, and plat — establish the specific governance rules for each association.
explanations.b: The Georgia Real Estate License Act governs licensees; it does not create condominium governance structures.
explanations.c: The NAR Code of Ethics governs REALTOR® conduct; it has no role in establishing condominium governance.
explanations.d: While a federal act exists, Georgia condominium associations are governed by state law, primarily the Georgia Condominium Act.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.keyword: unlicensed CAM cannot manage for compensation
questions.text: A person who manages a Georgia community association for compensation without holding a valid CAM license is:

answers.text: permitted to manage up to three associations without a license under a small-portfolio exemption
allowed to manage if supervised by a licensed real estate broker
in violation of Georgia license law and subject to criminal and civil penalties
exempt if the association has fewer than 50 units

explanations.a: There is no small-portfolio exemption from the CAM licensing requirement under Georgia law.
explanations.b: A real estate broker's supervision does not substitute for the specific CAM license required to manage community associations for compensation.
explanations.c: Managing a community association for compensation without a valid Georgia CAM license violates O.C.G.A. § 43-40 and exposes the individual to criminal prosecution and civil liability.
explanations.d: There is no unit-count exemption from the CAM licensing requirement; the license is required regardless of portfolio size.

questions.name: Real Estate Practice in Georgia
questions.text: The Georgia Community Association Manager examination differs from the Salesperson examination in that the CAM examination:

answers.text: includes both a national portion and a Georgia supplement, just like the salesperson exam
is administered only once per year at the GREC offices in Atlanta
requires a score of 75% or higher on each section to pass
consists entirely of Georgia-specific content with no national portion

explanations.a: Unlike the salesperson exam, the CAM exam does not have a separate national portion; it tests only Georgia-specific content.
explanations.b: CAM exams are administered at AMP Assessment Centers on the same schedule as salesperson exams — Monday through Saturday by appointment.
explanations.c: The specific pass score for the CAM exam is determined by the Angoff method, not a fixed 75% threshold; see the candidate handbook for exact passing requirements.
explanations.d: The Community Association Manager examination covers only Georgia law and practice topics and does not include a national real estate portion.
